summary: Defines inetOrgPerson, an LDAP object class for describing a person in an organization's directory. It extends the X.521 organizationalPerson class with attributes commonly needed for Internet and intranet use. It is an informational memo, and later RFCs update it.

plainLanguage.summary: A company phone book needs a standard form for each person. This defines a form with the boxes people on the Internet usually need, like email and name, so every directory fills it in the same way.

subtitle: A standard directory entry for a person in an organization, built for Internet and intranet use.

tldr.problem: The X.500 standards define many attribute types and object classes, but no person object class that meets what Internet and intranet directory deployments need.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a structural object class, inetOrgPerson, derived from the X.521 organizationalPerson class. It adds nine new attribute types, such as displayName, employeeNumber and userSMIMECertificate, and lists other attributes it can hold.
tldr.outcome: Using the class is optional. The RFC presents it as a well-documented class that implementers can choose to use. It is an Informational RFC that later RFCs have updated.

today: RFC 2798 is an Informational RFC. It has not been obsoleted, but it has been updated by RFC 3698, RFC 4519 and RFC 4524, so those should be read alongside it.

sections.title: Background and Intended Use
sections.content:
The inetOrgPerson object class is a general purpose class that holds attributes about people. The attributes were chosen to fit the information needs of typical Internet and intranet directory services. It is designed for directories based on LDAP (RFC 2251) and the X.500 family of protocols, and may be useful elsewhere.

There is no requirement for implementers to use it. It is simply presented as a well-documented class they can adopt if it is useful. Definitions are written using the BNF forms of AttributeTypeDescription and ObjectClassDescription from RFC 2252. Attributes the RFC uses but does not define come from RFC 1274, RFC 2079 and RFC 2256.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a ready-made contact card that any company can use if it wants, but nobody has to.

sections.title: The Nine New Attribute Types
sections.content:
Section 2 defines nine attribute types new to this class: carLicense, departmentNumber, displayName, employeeNumber, employeeType, jpegPhoto, preferredLanguage, userSMIMECertificate and userPKCS12.

Some choices are worth noting. displayName exists because other name attributes such as cn are multivalued, so an entry needs one name for one-line summary lists. employeeType typically holds values like Contractor, Employee, Intern, Temp, External and Unknown, but any value may be used. preferredLanguage values must follow the Accept-Language header syntax of RFC 2068, without the leading header name and colon. jpegPhoto stores JPEG images; the RFC notes that no referencable definition of it could be located.

The two certificate attributes are stored and requested in binary form, as userSMIMECertificate;binary and userPKCS12;binary. The S/MIME attribute holds a PKCS#7 SignedData with the person's certificate chain, and is preferred over userCertificate for S/MIME applications when available.
sections.plainLanguage: The new boxes on the form are things like a nickname to show on screens, an employee number, a photo, and a language the person likes to use.

sections.title: The inetOrgPerson Object Class
sections.content:
inetOrgPerson represents people who are associated with an organization in some way. It is a structural class with object identifier 2.16.840.1.113730.3.2.2, derived from organizationalPerson as defined in X.521.

Its own attribute list is all optional (MAY). It covers things like mail, uid, mobile, homePhone, manager, secretary and labeledURI, plus the nine new types. Inherited from organizationalPerson and person are three required attributes, cn, objectClass and sn, and many optional ones such as telephoneNumber, title and userPassword. An appendix summarizes every attribute type, syntax and matching rule involved.
sections.plainLanguage: The form starts from the basic person form and adds extra optional boxes. Only a name and a family name are required.

sections.title: An Example Entry
sections.content:
The RFC gives an example entry for Barbara Jensen written in LDIF. It names the entry with a distinguished name, lists the object classes top, person, organizationalPerson and inetOrgPerson, and fills in values such as two cn values, a displayName, a title, phone numbers, a carLicense, a departmentNumber and a preferredLanguage.

The example shows how the inherited and the new attributes sit together in one entry.
sections.plainLanguage: The example is a filled-in form for one pretend person, showing every box in use.

sections.title: Privacy and Password Cautions
sections.content:
The security section is short. Directory attributes describe real-world objects, which can be people, organizations or devices, and most countries have privacy laws about publishing information about people.

It also strongly discourages sending cleartext passwords where the underlying transport cannot guarantee confidentiality, since that may disclose the password to unauthorized parties.
sections.plainLanguage: A phone book full of personal details needs care: do not share people's information carelessly, and do not shout passwords across the room.

items.label: Vehicle plate
items.desc: Vehicle license or registration plate; multivalued.

items.label: Department
items.desc: Identifies a department within an organization.

items.label: Display name
items.desc: Preferred name to use when displaying entries; single-valued.

items.label: Employee type
items.desc: Type of employment, such as Contractor or Intern.

items.label: Photo
items.desc: One or more JPEG images of a person.

items.label: Language
items.desc: Preferred written or spoken language; single-valued.

items.label: S/MIME certificate
items.desc: PKCS#7 SignedData used to support S/MIME.

items.label: PKCS #12
items.desc: PFX PDU for exchange of personal identity information.
